title: Fruits Highest in Sugar

seo.title: Fruits Highest in Sugar per 100 Grams
seo.meta_description: Among common fresh fruits, grapes and figs are near 16 g sugar per 100 g, followed by pomegranate, mango, sweet cherries, and bananas. Portion size matters too.
seo.search_intent: Compare sugar content of fresh fruits with numbers per 100 grams and realistic serving context.

excerpt: Among commonly eaten fresh fruits, grapes and fresh figs are around 16 g of sugars per 100 g, pomegranate and mango around 13–14 g, sweet cherries around 13 g, and bananas around 12 g. Dried fruit is a separate category because removing water greatly concentrates sugar.
content_html:
Calling a fruit “high in sugar” without numbers is not very useful. A fair comparison uses grams of total sugars per 100 g of edible fresh fruit, while remembering that variety and ripeness shift the exact values.

Fresh fruits that tend to rank high

FruitApprox. sugars per 100 g
Fresh figs~16 g
Grapes~16 g
Pomegranate arils~14 g
Mango~14 g
Sweet cherries~13 g
Banana~12 g

These are rounded values from composition databases such as USDA FoodData Central, not fixed numbers for every cultivar.

Dried fruit belongs in a different comparison

Raisins and dates lose much of their water, concentrating everything else. Dried fruit can contain more than 50–60 g of sugars per 100 g, so putting it in the same ranking as fresh oranges or berries answers a different question.

Serving size changes the picture

A 100 g portion of grapes is fairly small by volume. Eat 200 g of a fruit containing 8 g sugar per 100 g and you still consume 16 g total. Density and portion size matter together.

Fruit sugar is not the same as added sugar

Whole fruit provides water, fiber, vitamins, minerals, and plant compounds alongside its naturally occurring sugars. That does not make carbohydrate amount irrelevant for people who need to track it, but nutritionally it is not identical to adding the same grams of sugar to a drink.

Use per-100-g values to compare foods; use your actual serving size to understand what you eat.

faq.question: Which fresh fruits have the most sugar?
faq.answer: Commonly eaten fresh grapes and figs are among the higher options at roughly 16 g sugars per 100 g.

faq.question: Does mango have more sugar than banana?
faq.answer: On average, yes: mango is around 14 g per 100 g while banana is closer to 12 g.

faq.question: Why are raisins so much higher?
faq.answer: Drying removes water and concentrates sugar, so dried fruit should be compared separately from fresh fruit.
